conviction_note: Evidence leans mildly negative and agrees with the +13.9 vol-point put skew: Q1 missed the company's OWN guide on both sales and margin, plant-consolidation friction was said to persist all year, and furniture-store demand in Aug-Oct was soft (NRF -2.7%/-2.6%, Havertys written +1.7% with traffic down MSD). Against that, Q1 retail written (+16%) ran well ahead of delivered (+10%) into Q2, the written-comp base is easy (-2% LY), and the stock is 25% below the mean target after slipping 4.8% into the print. Findings sum to -1.3; the scaled number is p_up 45 x abs 12.5 = -1.25. The two agree because nothing found is a decisive unpriced company number; the move will be set by the new Q3 guide, which none of the evidence pins down.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 Retail written sales grew +16% while Retail delivered sales grew only +10% (to $229m), and management said the Wholesale backlog was 'solid entering the second quarter'; written running ~6pp ahead of delivered builds a retail delivery backlog that supports Q2 delivered sales at or above the $510m guide midpoint the street ($507-512m) is sitting on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales beat in Nov 2025 ($522.5m vs $517.6m, with an EPS beat) bought +20.2%; the sales miss in Aug 2026 ($476m vs $499.7m and below own guide) sold -17.0%. Sales against guide is a line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The written-vs-delivered gap is in the release but the street revenue estimate ($506.9-511.7m) sits at or below the guide midpoint rather than above it; if the backlog were priced, estimates would sit toward the top of the $500-520m range. Partly priced: it is inside the guide the company already gave.
findings.independence: Same release as finding 2 and 3 (one document). Different source pointing the same way: Q1 call said 'our backlog is solid entering the second quarter' (https://www.webull.com/news/15429759208276992).

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 missed the company's OWN guide on both lines (sales $476m vs $490-510m guided in June; adj op margin 3.9% vs 4.0-5.5%), and on the Q1 call management said plant-consolidation 'friction cost versus expectations' would 'remain for the balance of the year' with the second plant closing by fiscal year-end; the Q2 guide (4-5.5%) carries the same cost structure, so a second below-range quarter is a live risk the street at the $0.48 midpoint does not discount.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 below-guide quarter plus a below-street guide fell -16.95%; the Feb 2026 print (adj EPS $0.61, cautious Q4 guide) fell -6.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($0.48), i.e. the street is taking the guide at face value despite the Q1 miss of the guide; if the credibility discount were priced, estimates would sit toward the low end (~$0.40). The stock's -17% in August priced the lower guide, not a second miss of it. The Q1 margin guide figure comes from a Zacks summary of the June release, not read directly.
findings.independence: Q1 actuals: https://finviz.com/news/383445/la-z-boy-incorporated-reports-first-quarter-results-retail-momentum-with-positive-written-same-store-sales ; friction-cost quote: https://www.webull.com/news/15429759208276992 (Q1 call transcript, 2026-08-19).

findings.finding: The Q2 written-comp base is easy: Q2 FY26 written same-store sales were -2% (with October 2025 the strongest month), against which Q1 FY27 already printed +3% written same-store, a 500bp sequential improvement; a positive written comp in Q2 is likely and is the retail metric management leads with.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positive written SSS (+3%) in Aug 2026 did not prevent -17% on the guide; the June 2026 print with comps turning positive in April-May rose +14.8% alongside a Q1 guide above street. The line helps only alongside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The comparison base is public, but no estimate of Q2 written comps is published, so the street cannot be shown to hold it; partly priced through the guide.

findings.finding: Q2 FY26's 7.1% adj operating margin included a one-time ~110bp benefit from a change in dealer warranty arrangements, so the guided 4-5.5% Q2 FY27 margin is a year-on-year drop of 160-310bp that will headline as a large decline even if it lands in range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior instance; the guided margin decline was the August reaction (-17%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the guide the company gave and in the consensus; filed for completeness, sized at zero.

findings.finding: The new Q3 FY27 guide has structural headwinds the street's ~$0.59 Q3 EPS (vs $0.61 a year ago) may not fully carry: the 15-store Southeast acquisition (~$80m/yr sales) closed at the end of October 2025 and stops contributing non-comp growth from Q3; the casegoods business (in last year's $542m Q3) is gone; plant friction persists through year-end; Joybird written -17% in Q1. Offset: easy comps and ~10 new stores a year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock: June 2026 Q1 guide above street +14.8%; Aug 2026 Q2 guide below street -17.0%; Feb 2026 cautious Q4 guide -6.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Street Q3 EPS is about flat year on year, implying a margin recovery that the plant-friction commentary and loss of the acquisition tailwind do not obviously support; a priced view would show Q3 estimates down year on year. Inference from public items, so sized small against a guide that moves this stock 15-20%.

findings.finding: Havertys (Southeast furniture retailer, reported 2026-11-04) said written sales rose only +1.7% across August-September with the Labor Day event flat, comp written +2.3% for Q3 vs +12.3% in Q2, and traffic swung to down mid-single digits; its stock fell 11.2% the next day.
findings.link: Same channel and overlapping geography: both are furniture retailers selling upholstery through own stores in the US Southeast (LZB's 15 acquired Atlanta/Orlando/Jacksonville/Knoxville stores), same Aug-Oct demand window; different brands, no shared customers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LZB fell only -1.3% on Nov 5 (XLY -3.8% that day) when Havertys dropped 11%, so the read-through was not taken at the time.
findings.why_not_priced: LZB did not react on Nov 5 and has risen since; a priced read-through would show LZB down with HVT. Peer proxy, not LZB's number.

findings.finding: CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor: furniture and home furnishings stores were the only major category down year on year in September 2026 (-2.7%) and fell again in October (-2.62%) while total retail rose 3.57%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none sourced for LZB on this series
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series; LZB's 20-day +6.8% suggests it is not being read into this name. Macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company; LZB's Q1 written comp was +3% against a soft category.
findings.independence: October figure: https://massmarketretailers.com/retail-sales-extend-winning-streak-to-13-months/ (secondary, 2026-11). Methodology changed in Sept 2026.

findings.finding: Ethan Allen (reported Nov 2026, quarter to Sep 30) said retail written orders fell -1.2% and wholesale -1.3% year on year, citing weaker design-center traffic and housing, with October retail orders +0.3%.
findings.link: Same product category (US-made upholstery and case goods sold mostly through own design centers); higher price point; no shared customers; overlapping Aug-Oct window.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer proxy; October stabilisation (+0.3%) partly offsets; small.

findings.finding: Flexsteel (US upholstery maker selling through independent furniture dealers) reported for the quarter to Sep 30, 2026 orders +5% and ending backlog +8.2% year on year, core brand sales +5.1%, and guided its Dec quarter to +1% to +4%.
findings.link: Same product (residential upholstery incl. motion/recliners) and same wholesale channel (independent dealers) as LZB's Wholesale segment (~$323m of Q1's $476m before eliminations); direct competitor, no shared customers sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The wholesale-upholstery demand read from Flexsteel is better than the retail-store series above; LZB's wholesale was -5% ex casegoods in Q1 with 'choppy' orders, so a firmer dealer channel is not in the Q2 guide's narrative. Peer proxy, small.

findings.finding: Bassett (quarter to Aug 29, reported 2026-09-30) reported retail written sales +4.4% despite one less Labor Day week, wholesale orders +7.9%, and a Labor Day event up 9%.
findings.link: Same category (US upholstery/case goods, own-store retail plus wholesale), overlapping Labor Day window; much smaller company; no shared customers.
findings.why_not_priced: Small peer, little read-through attention; contradicts Havertys' flat Labor Day, so the industry picture is mixed. Snippet only.

findings.finding: Arhaus reported (2026-11-05) comparable written sales +13.9% for Jul-Sep, up from +12.5% in Q2, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook.
findings.link: Same category (upholstery-led home furnishings via own showrooms), higher price point and affluent customer; weak link to LZB's middle-market buyer.
findings.why_not_priced: Different customer tier; half-price clearance events may have inflated orders (analyst note). Small.

findings.finding: Wayfair reported (2026-11-04) US revenue +11.4% in Q3 while describing the US home category as roughly flat, i.e. share gains rather than category recovery.
findings.link: Same category (furniture), online channel; Wayfair gaining share is partly at the expense of store-based sellers; weak link.
findings.why_not_priced: Points both ways (flat category, share shift to online); sized zero.

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds: LZB said it is 'in process' for refunds that are 'significantly less than others in our industry', and Q1 Wholesale margin already carried a 240bp favourable tariff impact including refunds; any Q2 refund in adjusted results risks the Havertys treatment (HVT fell 11% after the market stripped $3.2m of refunds out).

findings.why_not_priced: Amount undisclosed; no path to the guide sourced, so sized as a fraction.

findings.why_not_priced: It is priced as the bar; filed because a bar at midpoint removes the August-style 'guide below street' shock for the reported quarter. Snippet only (page 403).
